# Per-copy state two loops deep: each `outer` copy keeps its own `count`, and
# the handler its call site hands each `inner` -- which `inner`'s effect runs
# as its @mount's `done()` -- writes that copy's cell. On bubbletea both are
# cells per copy, and the effect is handed the whole copy key through `on`,
# the outer copy's index included: each copy's `count` reaches 2, not 6.

sngl test --platform=none app.sngl
stdout 'PASS'
! stdout 'FAIL'

sngl test --platform=bubbletea --language=go app.sngl
stdout 'PASS'
! stdout 'FAIL'

sngl test --platform=fyne --language=go app.sngl
stdout 'PASS'
! stdout 'FAIL'

sngl test --platform=html app.sngl
stdout 'PASS'
! stdout 'FAIL'

-- app.sngl --
import ui "sngl:ui"
import "sngl:test"

component inner(@done()) ui.node {
    var x = 0
    effect(@mount {
        x = x + 1
        done()
    })
}

component outer(@done(count int)) ui.node {
    var count = 0
    ui.vbox {
        for var j = [1, 2] {
            inner(@done {
                count += 1
                done(count)
            })
        }
    }
}

component nest ui.node {
    var items = [1, 2, 3]
    var mounts = 0
    var peak = 0
    ui.vbox {
        for var i = items {
            outer(@done(n) {
                mounts += 1
                if n > peak {
                    peak = n
                }
            })
        }
    }
}

func testEachOuterCopyCountsItsOwn(t test.Test, c nest) {
    t.assert(c.mounts == 6)
    t.assert(c.peak == 2)
}
